transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Um, hi. My manager told me I had to come in. It's... well, it's because of work. I'm a waitress, and what scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service. Or doing things totally out of order. 

Like, the other day I was standing by the soda station... we just got one of those new machines where you can touch the screen for all the different flavors? I always liked mixing the cherry and the vanilla. It reminds me of this diner I used to go to when I was taking classes at the community college, they had the absolute best floats. We'd go there after my art history lab. 

But anyway, I was just standing there by the ice dispenser, holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. Table four, table nine... I think nine had ordered the tuna melt, they always ask for extra pickles. But yeah, I was just standing there frozen with the key. It's on one of those stretchy plastic coil bracelets, you know? The blue ones. It always pinches the little hairs on my wrist if I'm not careful.
When you freeze up like that at work, is it mainly because your mind is wandering or you’re getting distracted?

I wouldn't say I'm getting distracted, exactly. It's more like... well, like I was just saying, I end up doing things completely out of order, or I just freeze up right in the middle of service. I know I'm supposed to be closing out the checks, but instead I'm just standing there by the soda station with that key, repeating the numbers. 

But if you say a number too many times, it stops sounding like a real word, you know? Like "four." Four, four, four. It almost sounds like a dog barking if you say it fast. My neighbor has a dog, this little scruffy terrier mix, I think. It barks every single morning at exactly 6:00 AM when the garbage truck comes down our alley. Those trucks are so incredibly loud, they have those big hydraulic arms that lift the green bins right up into the air. I always kind of wanted to pull the lever on one of those. It seems like it would be really satisfying, just crushing all that trash. I wonder if the drivers get to listen to the radio while they do it.
Have you had problems like this since you were a child?

No, no, not since I was a kid. I was actually a really focused kid, I used to sit for hours organizing my colored pencils by shade. But this whole... change in me, it's been building for about a year and two months. That's when my manager asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. 

I didn't really want to do the evening shift because that's when the bus schedule gets weird. The number 42 bus stops running at 10:30 PM, and if I miss it, I have to wait for the night owl route, which takes twice as long because it loops all the way past the old shopping mall. They're tearing that mall down, actually. I saw the wrecking ball out there last week. It's sad, I bought my first pair of roller skates there. They were white with these bright pink wheels, and I used to skate up and down my driveway until the streetlights came on. They had this really strong smell of new leather and plastic, you know? Like a new car, but sweeter. I wonder what happens to all the mannequins when a mall closes. Do they just throw them in the dumpster? That would look so creepy, just a bunch of plastic arms and legs sticking out of the trash.
Do you avoid social situations because you’re afraid of being judged or rejected by other people?

No, it's not really about being judged. I mean, I don't think about people judging me. I just... I don't really go out much anyway. I usually just go to work and come home. It's easier that way, especially with the bus schedule being so weird like I said. 

Plus, when I get home, I really just want to take my shoes off. Being on your feet all day on that hard tile floor... they make us wear these slip-resistant shoes, which I get, because the kitchen floor is always wet near the dish pit. The dishwasher, his name is Hector, he always plays his music really loud on this little Bluetooth speaker. It's usually salsa music. It's got a really good beat, actually. Sometimes I catch myself tapping my foot to it while I'm waiting for my orders in the window. The heat lamps in the window are so intense, though. They always make the back of my neck sweat if I stand there too long. I bought this special cooling towel once from a sporting goods store, you're supposed to get it wet and snap it, and it stays cold for hours. It was bright green, almost neon. I wonder where I put that towel. I think I might have left it in my locker at work, but the locker door is kind of jammed. The latch gets stuck if you push it too hard.
Do you usually prefer being alone rather than spending time with other people?

I suppose I do. Or, well, it's just what ends up happening. Like, when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. It just feels like I can’t get myself to care or start anything. I don’t really go for beach walks, or bake, or garden, or write in my journal much anymore either. 

I used to write in my journal every single night with this specific blue gel pen. It had this really nice rubber grip on it. I hate pens that make your fingers cramp up. My husband always buys those cheap bulk pens from the office supply store, the ones with the clear plastic caps that always crack if you chew on them. I used to chew on my pen caps all the time when I was taking classes at the community college. I had this art history class where the professor would show slides in the dark, and the projector made this continuous humming noise. It sounded exactly like the refrigerator in our apartment right before the compressor died last summer. We lost a whole freezer full of blueberries when that happened. I was actually going to use them to bake some muffins, but they just melted into this giant, sticky purple puddle at the bottom of the drawer. Blueberry stains are really hard to get out of plastic. You have to use baking soda and vinegar, and it bubbles up like a little science fair volcano. I always liked those volcano projects, the way the red food coloring stains the papier-mâché.
Were you having similar problems with distractibility or acting out of order when you were a child?

No, not at all. Like I was saying earlier, I was actually really focused. I didn't act out or get distracted. I would just sit quietly and do my own thing. In second grade, my teacher, Mrs. Gable, had this huge glass jar of vintage buttons, and she would let me sort them by size and color whenever it rained during recess. 

I really liked the heavy metal ones the best. They had these intricate little anchors stamped on them, like they belonged on a ship captain's coat. I went on a ferry boat once when I was little, and the wind was so loud you couldn't even hear yourself think. The water was this dark, murky green color, and it kept churning up white foam at the back of the boat. Sea foam is so weird, it looks exactly like soap suds but it smells like salt and seaweed. I tried to make homemade soap once during the pandemic. You have to use lye, which is actually really dangerous if you get it on your skin. It gets super hot when you mix it with water, like boiling hot. You have to wear these thick rubber gloves, the kind people use for washing dishes. I always buy the yellow ones, but they get holes in the fingertips so fast. Then the water seeps in and your hands smell like old dishwater for the rest of the day. It's the worst smell, especially when you've been scrubbing plates with dried egg yolk on them. Egg yolk is basically like cement if you don't soak it right away.
In the past year, have you been feeling worried or anxious most days?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I don't feel worried about things most days. I just kind of exist, you know? Just go through the motions. Like yesterday, I was just staring out the window for a while. 

There's this bird feeder outside our apartment window, the plastic tube kind with the little perches. We usually get these tiny gray birds, chickadees I think they're called. They're so fast, they just dart in, grab a seed, and fly away. But lately the squirrels have figured out how to climb down the hook it hangs from. They are so greedy. One squirrel hung upside down by its back feet and just stuffed its cheeks until they were bulging out like golf balls. My husband tried putting cayenne pepper in the birdseed because birds can't taste spice but mammals can, but I don't know if it worked. The pepper smells really strong, kind of like the paprika they use at work for the deviled eggs. We only serve deviled eggs on the Sunday brunch menu, and they take forever to prep. You have to peel like a hundred hard-boiled eggs, and if they're too fresh, the shells stick to the egg whites and tear them up. Then they look all jagged and terrible on the plate, and Chef gets really mad. He yells so loud his face turns red, like, this blotchy tomato color.
Have you always been shy and held back around other people, even before this past year?

No, I don't think I was always shy. I mean, I wasn't really the one holding back or anything. I just... I don't know, I didn't really have a problem talking to people before. I used to talk to the customers at work all the time, especially the regulars. 

There was this one older couple, they came in every Tuesday at 4:30 right before the dinner rush started. The husband always ordered a patty melt with extra onions, and he would tell me these really long stories about his time in the Navy. He said the food on the ships was mostly out of cans, like canned peaches and baked beans. I really hate baked beans. They're so sweet, it's like eating dessert for dinner. And the sauce always gets everywhere, it stains the white plates if you don't rinse them right away. The dishwasher at work is this huge industrial machine, it sounds like an airplane taking off when it runs. The steam comes pouring out when you lift the door, and it fogs up my glasses instantly. I hate having to wipe them on my apron because the apron always has flour or grease on it from the kitchen. Grease is impossible to get out of clothes. You have to use that blue dish soap, the one with the little duck on the bottle. They use that on ducks when there's an oil spill in the ocean. It's so sad seeing those poor birds covered in black sludge. They look so heavy, like they can't even lift their wings.
Over the past year, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?

I don't think so, no. I haven't really been feeling sad or depressed. I just kind of... I don't know, I just feel fine, I guess. Not down. But speaking of down, I did have to go down into the basement at work a lot recently to get the extra roll-ups. We roll the silverware in these heavy cloth napkins, and they keep the spare ones in these big plastic bins downstairs. 

The stairs are so steep and the light bulb at the bottom keeps flickering. It's one of those long fluorescent tubes that hums really loud. It sounds exactly like the refrigerator in my apartment. My fridge has this weird rattle every time the ice maker kicks on. It drops the ice into the plastic tray with this huge clatter in the middle of the night. I don't even use ice that much anyway, it makes my teeth hurt. My dentist told me I need to use that special toothpaste for sensitive teeth, the one in the green tube. But it tastes like chalk and wintergreen. Wintergreen is the absolute worst flavor, it reminds me of those pink mints they give you with the check at that diner down the street. They're so chalky, they just dissolve in your mouth like dust. And they always leave that weird powdery feeling on your tongue that won't go away even if you drink a whole glass of water.
When you’re around other people, do you often hold back because you’re afraid they’ll criticize or judge you?

No, I don't really hold back because I'm scared they'll judge me. I mean, I just don't really talk to them that much anyway. I don't think they're criticizing me. They're usually just looking at their phones or whatever. 

Everyone is always looking at their phones now. Even at the restaurant, you'll get a whole family of four at a table, and they're all just staring at their screens while they eat. It's so weird. They don't even look up when I refill their water glasses. The water pitchers we use are made of this thick, heavy plastic, and they get so slippery from the condensation. Last week, I almost dropped one right onto this lady's lap. She had this really nice silk blouse on, this bright emerald green color. I love that color, it reminds me of the sea glass I used to find on the beach when I was a kid. We used to go to this beach up in Maine, and the water was always freezing, even in August. You could only go in up to your ankles before your toes went completely numb. And the sand was full of these sharp little broken shells that would cut your feet if you weren't careful. My mom used to make us wear those ugly water shoes, the ones made of that squishy neoprene material. They always got filled with sand and took three days to dry out on the porch railing.
When these episodes happen, do you ever lose time or later not remember what you were doing?

No, I don't think I lose time or anything like that. I usually remember what I'm doing. Like, I always know where I am and what's going on. I don't just forget. 

But sometimes I forget where I put my keys. I have this little bowl by the door, it's shaped like a seashell, but I never actually put them in there. I always end up tossing them on the kitchen counter next to the microwave. The microwave has this really annoying beep when it finishes heating something up. It's so loud, it echoes all the way down the hallway. It beeps five times, exactly five times, and you can't stop it once it starts, even if you open the door. I tried looking up how to mute it online, but the manual is like a hundred pages long and it's all in different languages. I don't understand why they have to print it in so many languages in one book. They should just give you the English one. It wastes so much paper. And paper is getting so expensive now. Even the little receipt paper rolls at the restaurant cost twice as much as they did last year. The manager was complaining about it the other day when he was changing the roll in the register. He always struggles to get the paper to feed through the little slot properly. It always jams up and prints all the letters on top of each other in this big black smudge.
Do you avoid being around other people because you’re afraid they’ll criticize, embarrass, or reject you?

No, I don't really avoid people because I'm scared they'll reject me or anything. Like I said, I just don't talk to them much anyway. It's not about being embarrassed, I just do my own thing. 

Speaking of doing my own thing, I finally got around to organizing my closet yesterday. I have all these wire hangers from the dry cleaners, the thin ones that always get tangled up together. I tried to group them by color, but most of them are just that weird white coating that peels off at the corners. When it peels, the metal underneath is all rusty and it leaves these little brown marks on the shoulders of my shirts. I have this one favorite shirt, it's a cotton button-down, and it got a rust stain right on the collar. I tried using that stain remover pen, the one that smells like harsh chemicals, but it just made the stain spread out into a bigger, lighter brown circle. It looked like a coffee stain after that. People spill coffee all the time at work, especially during the Sunday brunch rush. They order these huge mugs of dark roast and then wave their hands around while they're talking and just knock it right over. The coffee seeps into the tablecloths so fast, you have to throw a whole stack of napkins on it immediately or it drips onto the floor. And the floor in the dining room is that dark wood laminate, so you can't even tell it's wet until you step in it and your shoe makes that sticky, squelching sound for the rest of your shift. It drives me crazy, that sound. It's like walking on tape.
Have you felt this way in most areas of your life for as long as you can remember, or did it start only in the past year?

Well, no, not for as long as I can remember. This whole change in me has really just been building for about a year and two months. That's when they asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities at the restaurant. 

The evening shift is completely different from the morning rush. Right at 5:00 PM, we have to go around and light all these little tea candles for the tables. They come in these frosted glass holders, and by the end of the night, the wax is completely melted into this little liquid pool. If you blow them out too hard, the hot wax splatters up the sides of the glass and hardens instantly. Then the next day, you have to sit there with a butter knife and scrape it all off before you can put a new candle in. The butter knives we have are so dull, though. You couldn't even cut a piece of bread with them, let alone the steaks they serve. People always ask for a real steak knife, and we keep them in this wooden block back in the server alley. The wood block is supposed to be sanitized, but it just gets sticky from everyone grabbing it with syrup or dressing on their hands. We have this one vinaigrette, a raspberry walnut one, and it stains everything it touches bright pink. It looks exactly like the cough syrup my grandmother used to make me take when I was little. It came in a glass bottle with a metal cap that always got stuck, so she'd have to run it under hot water just to twist it off.
When you're with other people, do you usually feel afraid that they'll judge, criticize, or reject you?

I don't think so. I mean, you asked me that a minute ago, right? About people rejecting me? No, I don't really worry about them judging me or anything. Like I said, I mostly just keep to myself anyway. 

Keeping to myself is easier, especially when I'm walking home from work. The streetlights on my route are always flickering. There's this one light right at the corner of Elm and 4th, and it buzzes. It's this really low, electrical hum, like a giant bee trapped inside the glass. Sometimes it completely goes out for a few seconds, and it gets pitch black right there because the trees block the moonlight. The city planted these huge oak trees along the sidewalk, and the roots are pushing up all the concrete slabs. You have to be really careful not to trip, especially if you're wearing those non-slip work shoes. The tread on the bottom is supposed to keep you from falling on grease, but they grab onto the edge of the broken sidewalk and just stop your foot dead. My coworker tripped last week and dropped her whole bag. She had this glass water bottle in there, one of those expensive ones with the silicone sleeve, and it shattered everywhere. The silicone didn't protect it at all. It just held all the broken glass pieces together like a puzzle you can't take apart. We had to use a broom from the patio to sweep it into the gutter so nobody's dog would step on it. People walk their dogs so late around here, usually those little fluffy ones that bark at everything.
Do you actually want close relationships with other people, or are you generally fine not having them?

I don't really want them, I guess. I'm generally fine without them. It's just... I don't really do much of anything anymore. I used to go for walks on the beach, bake, garden, write in my journal... but not really anymore. And when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. It feels like I can't get myself to care or start anything, you know? 

Speaking of starting things, I tried to start my car yesterday and the battery was completely dead. It's one of those older sedans, the kind where the key actually turns in the ignition instead of just pushing a button. I had to call my neighbor to give me a jump, and he brought over these jumper cables that were so tangled up they looked like a giant red and black snake. We had to untangle them on the driveway, and the clamps were covered in this weird white powdery stuff from battery acid. It gets all over your hands and you have to wash them immediately or it burns. I used this heavy-duty pumice soap we keep in the garage. It has these little gritty pieces in it, like sand, and it smells intensely like oranges. The smell is so strong it lingers on your skin for hours, even after you put lotion on. I have this one lotion, it's supposed to be unscented, but it actually smells a little bit like wet cardboard. It comes in a pump bottle, and when you get near the bottom, the pump can't reach the rest of it, so you have to unscrew the top and bang the bottle against your hand to get it out. It always splatters everywhere when you do that, mostly on the bathroom mirror. And then you have to clean the mirror with glass cleaner, which always leaves streaks unless you use a newspaper instead of paper towels.
Do you feel this same kind of difficulty in situations that aren’t social, like when you’re alone doing other tasks?

Yeah, like I was just saying a minute ago, it's definitely when I'm alone, too. It’s not just when my husband is trying to talk to me. I don't really bake or garden or write in my journal anymore, and I used to love doing all that by myself. I don't even go for my beach walks because I just can't get myself to care or start any of it. 

The beach is usually so windy anyway. Last time I went, I found this piece of sea glass that was perfectly smooth, like a little frosted green triangle. It probably came from one of those old soda bottles they used to make. They don't make them out of real glass as much anymore, mostly just that cheap plastic. Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down in the ocean, you know. I saw this program once about how sea turtles think plastic grocery bags are jellyfish, so they eat them. Jellyfish are actually mostly water, like ninety-five percent water, which is crazy to think about because they can sting you so badly. My cousin got stung by one when we were kids, and my aunt made him pour white vinegar all over his leg right there on the boardwalk. The smell of vinegar is just so overpowering. I have to use it sometimes to descale the big industrial coffee pot at the restaurant, but no matter how many times you rinse it out, the first batch of coffee you brew afterwards always tastes a little bit sour. People complain about it, but they still drink it if you put enough cream in it. We use those little plastic creamer cups that you have to peel the foil off of, and the foil always tears right down the middle instead of coming off in one piece.
When you’re around other people, do you often worry that they’ll criticize you?

I mean, no, not really. I think you asked me that already, didn't you? About people criticizing me? Yeah, I don't really worry about that. Like I said before, I just keep to myself mostly. 

It's just easier that way, especially at the restaurant. We have this one regular customer who comes in every Tuesday and orders a Cobb salad, but he wants the bacon on the side, the egg whites only, and the dressing in a separate little ramekin. Those ramekins are so hard to wash because they're tiny and the industrial dishwasher sprays water so hard it flips them over. When they flip over, they fill up with this gross, soapy, gray water that smells like old food and sanitizer. The sanitizer we use comes in these huge blue jugs that weigh like forty pounds. You have to heave them up onto this shelf above the sink, and the shelf is made of wire racks that dig into your hands. I have this callus on my thumb from grabbing those racks. It's rough, kind of like the skin on a lemon. Lemons are so expensive right now, we had to start cutting the wedges thinner for the iced tea. People get so mad when they don't get a big enough lemon wedge. They squeeze it and get juice all over their fingers, and then they wipe it on the cloth napkins. The linen company that washes the napkins must use bleach, because sometimes the dark blue ones come back with these weird pinkish spots on them.
Before this past year, did you also tend to feel inadequate or like you didn’t measure up compared with other people?

No, I don't think I ever really felt like that. I never really worried about measuring up to anyone else. 

Measuring things is actually really tricky though, like at work we have to measure the vanilla syrup for the milkshakes using these little metal jiggers. The metal gets freezing cold because we keep them right next to the ice cream freezer. That freezer has a broken seal on the door, so all this frost builds up on the outside, and it grows into these patterns that look exactly like tiny white fern leaves. I tried to scrape the ice off with a butter knife once, but the knife just bent backwards. The silverware at the restaurant is so flimsy. My grandmother had a set of real silver butter knives that were so heavy, and she kept them in this dark wooden box lined with red velvet. I hate touching velvet, it makes my teeth feel weird, kind of like when you accidentally bite down on a piece of aluminum foil. You know, like the foil they wrap baked potatoes in. If you leave a potato in the oven too long, the bottom gets completely black and hard as a rock, and it smells like a campfire in the kitchen.
Have you generally been uncomfortable or nervous around people since you were a young adult?

No, I don't think so. I've never really been nervous around people, even when I was younger. I mean, I've always been pretty okay with it. 

I guess maybe when I first started waiting tables, I was a little nervous about dropping things. You have to carry these huge oval trays that are made of this weird brown fiberglass material. The fiberglass gets all scratched up on the bottom from sliding across the metal pass where the cooks put the food. The pass has these heat lamps hanging over it, and the bulbs are giant and red. They get so hot that if you stand under them for too long, your hair starts to smell like it's burning. I burned my arm on a heat lamp once, right above my wrist, and it left a scar that looks exactly like a little crescent moon. I used to stare at the moon a lot when I was a kid. My dad got me this telescope for my tenth birthday, but the tripod was missing a rubber foot, so it always wobbled on the deck. The deck was made of this treated lumber that would give you the worst splinters if you walked on it barefoot. Splinters are so hard to get out, especially when they break off right under the skin. You have to use a needle and tweezers, and it always bleeds a tiny bit, just a little red dot.
When you’re around other people, do you feel afraid that they’ll think badly of you?

No, I don't think I worry about that. Like, people thinking badly of me? Not really. It's not something I spend time thinking about. 

I do think a lot about time, though. We have this huge clock on the wall in the breakroom at work, and the second hand makes this really loud ticking noise. Tick, tick, tick. It drives me crazy when I'm trying to eat my lunch. My lunch break is only thirty minutes, which barely gives me enough time to eat my sandwich. I always bring a turkey sandwich on rye bread. The rye bread has those little caraway seeds in it, and they always get stuck in my teeth. I have this one tooth in the back that has a tiny gap next to it, and everything gets caught there. I went to the dentist last year, and the waiting room had these awful fluorescent lights that buzzed. They sounded just like a swarm of bees. I got stung by a bee once when I was picking strawberries at this farm near my aunt's house. The strawberries were so red and sweet, but the juice stained my fingers for days. I tried scrubbing them with soap, but it didn't work. The soap we use at the restaurant is pink and smells like fake cherries. It comes out of the dispenser in these weird, foamy blobs that look like cotton candy.

patient.answer:
Um, hi. My manager told me I had to come in. It's... well, it's because of work. I'm a waitress, and what scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service. Or doing things totally out of order. 

Like, the other day I was standing by the soda station... we just got one of those new machines where you can touch the screen for all the different flavors? I always liked mixing the cherry and the vanilla. It reminds me of this diner I used to go to when I was taking classes at the community college, they had the absolute best floats. We'd go there after my art history lab. 

But anyway, I was just standing there by the ice dispenser, holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. Table four, table nine... I think nine had ordered the tuna melt, they always ask for extra pickles. But yeah, I was just standing there frozen with the key. It's on one of those stretchy plastic coil bracelets, you know? The blue ones. It always pinches the little hairs on my wrist if I'm not careful.

doctor.question: When you freeze up like that at work, is it mainly because your mind is wandering or you’re getting distracted?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior

patient.answer:
I wouldn't say I'm getting distracted, exactly. It's more like... well, like I was just saying, I end up doing things completely out of order, or I just freeze up right in the middle of service. I know I'm supposed to be closing out the checks, but instead I'm just standing there by the soda station with that key, repeating the numbers. 

But if you say a number too many times, it stops sounding like a real word, you know? Like "four." Four, four, four. It almost sounds like a dog barking if you say it fast. My neighbor has a dog, this little scruffy terrier mix, I think. It barks every single morning at exactly 6:00 AM when the garbage truck comes down our alley. Those trucks are so incredibly loud, they have those big hydraulic arms that lift the green bins right up into the air. I always kind of wanted to pull the lever on one of those. It seems like it would be really satisfying, just crushing all that trash. I wonder if the drivers get to listen to the radio while they do it.

doctor.question: When you’re around other people, do you feel afraid that they’ll think badly of you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about social anxiety/fear of negative evaluation, which is not covered by the patient's symptom profile (Delusions, Hallucinations, Disorganized/Abnormal Behavior, Negative Symptoms).

patient.answer:
No, I don't think I worry about that. Like, people thinking badly of me? Not really. It's not something I spend time thinking about. 

I do think a lot about time, though. We have this huge clock on the wall in the breakroom at work, and the second hand makes this really loud ticking noise. Tick, tick, tick. It drives me crazy when I'm trying to eat my lunch. My lunch break is only thirty minutes, which barely gives me enough time to eat my sandwich. I always bring a turkey sandwich on rye bread. The rye bread has those little caraway seeds in it, and they always get stuck in my teeth. I have this one tooth in the back that has a tiny gap next to it, and everything gets caught there. I went to the dentist last year, and the waiting room had these awful fluorescent lights that buzzed. They sounded just like a swarm of bees. I got stung by a bee once when I was picking strawberries at this farm near my aunt's house. The strawberries were so red and sweet, but the juice stained my fingers for days. I tried scrubbing them with soap, but it didn't work. The soap we use at the restaurant is pink and smells like fake cherries. It comes out of the dispenser in these weird, foamy blobs that look like cotton candy.
